offence_severity: Minimum 6 months to maximum 3 years imprisonment
number_of_offences: Two offences/counts charged and two were finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the FIR and the evidence of disproportionate assets held by the accused, including the construction of a house, purchase of a building, and transfer of property to the accused's minor son, which were deemed disproportionate to their known sources of income.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, including the investigating officer, as credible and noted that the explanation offered by the accused was not sufficient to dismiss the charge, as the burden of proof lay on the accused to account for the assets.
trial_duration: FIR registered on 19.09.2005; charge sheet filed; Special Judge rejected petition under s.239; High Court discharged respondents; Supreme Court allowed appeals, directed Special Court to frame charges and put accused to trial
legal_representation: V. Krishnamurthy, AAG, Dr. Joseph Aristotle S., Nupur Sharma, Shobhit Dwivedi, Sanjeev Kumar Mahara, Ms. Richa Vishwakarma, Advs. for the Appellant; K. Radhakrishnan, Sr. Adv., D. L. Chidananda, R. Janarthanan, S. Senthil Elangovan, S. Krishnamoorthy, K. Kumaravadivel, Advs. for the Respondents
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed; investigation completed; charge framed
appeal_history: Trial court: Discharged accused under s.239; High Court: Discharged accused; Supreme Court: Allowed appeals, set aside High Court orders, directed trial
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused, as a public servant, was in possession of properties disproportionate to his known sources of income, which are sources known to the prosecution, not the accused. The FIR was registered against the accused for offences under Section 13(2) read with 13(1)(e) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and the High Court's discharge order was challenged.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court had incorrectly discharged the accused, as the charge against them was not groundless. They claimed that the accused had provided satisfactory explanations for their assets and that the High Court had improperly considered the explanation offered by the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the burden of proof lies on the prosecution to establish that the accused was in possession of properties disproportionate to his known sources of income, which are sources known to the prosecution. The Court also emphasized that the stage of Section 239 of the CrPC requires a prima facie case to be considered, not a full evaluation of the evidence.
